newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: M&R sees 275 mln rand attrib year loss.
newsitem.headline: M&R sees 275 mln rand attrib year loss.

text.p: South African industrial group Murray & Roberts Ltd said on Tuesday that a series of one-off charges was likely to see it post an attributable loss of about 275 million rand for the year to June 30.
But the firm added that it was confident of maintaining its total dividend for the period.
The firm said in a statement that it had reassessed the impact of future losses on existing property headleases and made a provision of 130 million rand to cover the exposure.
It had also decided to reduce the carrying costs of various operations within Standard Engineering Ltd by 70 million rand.
M&R added that it had reached a settlement with Germany's Siemens AG on a contractual dispute over the supply of wagons to Taiwan's DORTS rapid transport system.
The firm said it had not yet ascribed a value to insurance claims related to the dipute, but that it had made certain provisions on other train contracts.
This would lead to a loss of 300 million rand on major train contracts in the second half of the financial year.
M&R said that its ongoing operations had performed well in the context of a tighter domestic market.

M&R said it had also reviewed its budget and forecasts for the next two financial years. It said it anticipated improvements in trading in 1998 and solid growth and continued cash generation in 1999 and 2000.
